entries.title: man <cmd>
entries.description: Full manual for a command (quit with q)

entries.title: info <cmd>
entries.description: More complete docs for some commands

entries.title: type <cmd>
entries.description: Command type: shell builtin, alias, or file

entries.title: hostname
entries.description: Print this machine's hostname (its name on the network).

entries.title: uptime
entries.description: How long the system is up + load average

entries.title: whoami
entries.description: Print the username you are currently logged in as.

entries.title: lscpu
entries.description: Show details about the CPU: model, cores, threads, speed and architecture.

entries.title: lspci
entries.description: List the hardware connected over PCI (graphics cards, network cards, storage controllers).

entries.title: lsusb
entries.description: List the USB devices currently plugged into this machine.

entries.title: echo $SHELL
entries.description: Print the shell you are using (for example, /bin/bash). Useful when a shortcut or script behaves differently than expected.

entries.title: uname -a && hostname && uptime && free -h
entries.description: A one-line system snapshot: kernel and machine info, hostname, how long the system has been up, and memory usage in human-readable form.

entries.title: ls
entries.description: List the files and folders in the current directory.

entries.title: ls -la
entries.description: Full list including hidden files and details

entries.title: cd -
entries.description: Go back to the previous directory

entries.title: touch <file>
entries.description: Create an empty file / update file time

entries.title: cp <src> <dst>
entries.description: Copy a file to a new location or a new name. The original stays where it is.

entries.title: mv <src> <dst>
entries.description: Move a file to another folder, or rename it when the destination is in the same folder. Moving within the same disk is instant.

entries.title: rm <file>
entries.description: Delete a file permanently (no trash, no undo). Double-check the name before pressing Enter.

entries.title: rm -r <dir>
entries.description: Delete a directory and its contents

entries.title: rm -rf <dir>
entries.description: Force delete without asking — be very careful

entries.title: file <file>
entries.description: Tell you what kind of file something really is (text, image, executable, archive), by looking at its contents instead of its extension.

entries.title: mkdir -p ~/project/{src,docs,tests} && cd ~/project && touch README.md
entries.description: Create a project skeleton in one go: the folders src, docs and tests, then move into it and create an empty README.md.

entries.title: less <file>
entries.description: Page-by-page viewer (q to quit, / to search)

entries.title: head -n 20 <file>
entries.description: Show only the first 20 lines of a file. Use it to peek at a file's start without opening the whole thing.

entries.title: tail -n 20 <file>
entries.description: Show only the last 20 lines of a file. The usual way to check the end of a log.

entries.title: wc -l <file>
entries.description: Count the number of lines in a file.

entries.title: wc -w <file>
entries.description: Count the number of words in a file.

entries.title: wc -c <file>
entries.description: Count the number of bytes in a file (roughly its size).

entries.title: grep -v "text" <file>
entries.description: Lines that do NOT contain the text

entries.title: grep -c "text" <file>
entries.description: Count how many lines in a file contain a phrase, instead of printing them.

entries.title: find . -type f -name "*.txt"
entries.description: Find every .txt file under the current folder, including subfolders.

entries.title: find . -mtime -7
entries.description: Files changed in the last 7 days

entries.title: locate <name>
entries.description: Fast search via database (updatedb to refresh it)

entries.title: sort <file>
entries.description: Print a file's lines sorted alphabetically.

entries.title: awk '{print $1}' <file>
entries.description: Print the first column of each line

entries.title: sed -i 's/old/new/g' <file>
entries.description: Replace text in the file itself

entries.title: grep -i "error" /var/log/syslog | tail -n 50
entries.description: Search the system log for 'error' (case-insensitive) and show only the last 50 matches — a fast way to see recent problems.

entries.title: du -ah ~ | sort -rh | head -n 10
entries.description: Find the 10 biggest things in your home folder: list every file and folder with its size, sort biggest first, show the top 10.

entries.title: chmod 600 <file>
entries.description: Only owner can read/write (e.g. SSH keys)

entries.title: chmod 700 <dir>
entries.description: Only owner can access the directory

entries.title: chgrp <group> <file>
entries.description: Change which group owns a file, so members of that group get the group's permissions on it.

entries.title: umask
entries.description: Show default permission mask for new files

entries.title: su -
entries.description: Switch to the root user with root's full environment (home, PATH, shell). You will be asked for root's password.

entries.title: su - <user>
entries.description: Switch to another user with full environment

entries.title: chmod +x deploy.sh && sudo chown www-data:www-data /var/www/html -R
entries.description: Make deploy.sh executable, then give the whole website folder to the www-data user and group (the web server), recursively — the standard web deploy permission fix.

entries.title: w
entries.description: Logged-in users + what they are doing

entries.title: last
entries.description: Show who logged in and out of this machine, and when — the login history from the system logs.

entries.title: last -n 10
entries.description: Show only the 10 most recent logins.

entries.title: id <user>
entries.description: ID and groups of a user

entries.title: sudo useradd -m -s /bin/bash <user>
entries.description: Create a user with home and shell

entries.title: sudo usermod -aG <group> <user>
entries.description: Add user to a group (keeps existing groups)

entries.title: sudo userdel <user>
entries.description: Delete a user account from the system (the user's files in /home stay unless you add -r).

entries.title: sudo userdel -r <user>
entries.description: Delete a user + their home directory

entries.title: sudo groupadd <group>
entries.description: Create a new group, so you can give several users the same permissions on shared files.

entries.title: sudo groupdel <group>
entries.description: Delete a group. It must have no members left (remove them first).

entries.title: getent passwd
entries.description: List every user account on this system, from all sources (local files, LDAP, and so on).

entries.title: sudo chage -l <user>
entries.description: Password expiry info for a user

entries.command: sudo useradd -m -s /bin/bash erfan && sudo passwd erfan && sudo usermod -aG sudo erfan
entries.title: sudo useradd -m -s /bin/bash erfan && sudo passwd erfan && sudo usermod -aG sudo erfan
entries.description: Create a user named erfan with a home folder and bash as the shell, set their password, and add them to the sudo group so they can run admin commands.
entries.example: sudo useradd -m -s /bin/bash erfan && sudo passwd erfan && sudo usermod -aG sudo erfan

entries.title: pidof nginx
entries.description: Only the PID of a process

entries.title: top
entries.description: Live view of processes and resource usage

entries.title: killall <name>
entries.description: Kill all processes of a name

entries.title: renice -n 5 -p <PID>
entries.description: Change priority of a running process

entries.title: fg
entries.description: Bring a job to the foreground

entries.title: bg
entries.description: Resume a stopped job in the background

entries.title: nohup <cmd> &
entries.description: Run even after the terminal closes

entries.title: disown
entries.description: Detach a job from the current shell

entries.title: wait <PID>
entries.description: Wait for a process to finish

entries.title: sudo ss -tlnp | grep 8080
entries.description: Check which process is listening on port 8080 (ss lists listening sockets with their processes; grep keeps only the 8080 line).

entries.title: umount /mnt
entries.description: Unmount a mounted disk or device from /mnt, so it can be safely removed.

entries.title: sudo mkfs.ext4 /dev/sdb1
entries.description: Format a partition (all data is erased)

entries.title: sudo swapon -s
entries.description: Show which swap areas are active and how much swap is in use.

entries.title: sudo mkswap /swapfile && sudo swapon /swapfile
entries.description: Format a file as swap space and turn it on, so the system can use it as extra (slow) memory when RAM runs out.

entries.title: ip route / ip r
entries.description: Show the routing table: where the system sends network traffic (the default gateway and the routes to other networks).

entries.title: curl -s https://api.ipify.org
entries.description: Ask an external service for your public IP address (the address the internet sees you as). The -s flag hides curl's progress output.

entries.title: dig example.com
entries.description: Ask the DNS servers for a domain's records (usually its IP address). Use it to check whether a domain resolves and where it points.

entries.title: host example.com
entries.description: Resolve a name to an IP

entries.title: traceroute example.com
entries.description: Route packets take to the destination

entries.title: ssh user@host
entries.description: Log in to a remote server

entries.title: ssh -p 2222 user@host
entries.description: Log in on a non-standard port

entries.title: scp file.txt user@host:/tmp/
entries.description: Copy a file to a server

entries.title: scp -r dir/ user@host:/tmp/
entries.description: Copy a directory to a server

entries.title: rsync -avz --delete src/ dst/
entries.description: Sync, deleting extra files at the destination

entries.title: sudo ss -tlnp | grep ':80'
entries.description: Check which process is listening on port 80 (the web port) — ss lists listening sockets with their processes, grep keeps only the :80 line.

entries.title: wget -c https://example.com/big.iso
entries.description: Download a file, with -c so an interrupted download resumes where it stopped instead of starting over.

entries.title: dpkg -l | grep <pkg>
entries.description: Check if a package is installed

entries.title: rpm -qa | grep <pkg>
entries.description: Check if a package is installed

entries.title: which <cmd> && <cmd> --version
entries.description: Check install and version of a tool

entries.title: systemctl status <svc>
entries.description: Show whether a systemd service is running, enabled, and its recent log lines.

entries.title: sudo systemctl stop <svc>
entries.description: Stop a running systemd service (it stays installed and can be started again).

entries.title: systemctl list-units --type=service
entries.description: List all systemd services on this machine with their load and active state.

entries.title: sudo systemctl daemon-reload
entries.description: Reload systemd units after editing a service file

entries.title: sudo systemctl mask <svc>
entries.description: Fully prevent a service from running

entries.title: sudo systemctl unmask <svc>
entries.description: Unmask a service that was masked (blocked from starting), so it can run again.

entries.command: sudo systemctl enable --now nginx && systemctl status nginx
entries.title: sudo systemctl enable --now nginx && systemctl status nginx
entries.description: Enable nginx to start at boot, start it right now, and then show its status to confirm it is running.
entries.example: sudo systemctl enable --now nginx && systemctl status nginx

entries.title: journalctl --since today
entries.description: Show the system journal's log entries from today onward.

entries.title: journalctl -p err
entries.description: Show only the journal entries at error level or worse, hiding informational messages.

entries.title: journalctl --disk-usage
entries.description: Show how much disk space the system journal's stored logs are using.

entries.command: sudo journalctl -u nginx -p err --since "1 hour ago"
entries.title: sudo journalctl -u nginx -p err --since "1 hour ago"
entries.description: Show nginx's error-level logs from the last hour — the first thing to check when a website is down.
entries.example: sudo journalctl -u nginx -p err --since "1 hour ago"

entries.title: sort file
entries.description: Print a file's lines sorted alphabetically.

entries.title: sort -n file
entries.description: Sort a file's lines as numbers (so 2 comes before 10), instead of alphabetically (where 10 comes before 2).

entries.title: sort -r file
entries.description: Sort a file's lines in reverse order (Z to A, or largest first).

entries.title: tr -d ' ' < file
entries.description: Delete every space character from a file's text and print the result.

entries.title: paste file1 file2
entries.description: Paste two files line by line

entries.title: join file1 file2
entries.description: Join two files on a common column

entries.title: tail -c 100 file
entries.description: Show the last 100 bytes of a file (not lines — bytes, so it can cut a line in half).

entries.title: xargs -I{} echo {} file
entries.description: Run a command on each input

entries.title: awk '{print $1}' /var/log/nginx/access.log | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head
entries.description: Find the most frequent visitor IPs in the nginx access log: take the first field (the IP) of every line, count duplicates, and show the most common ones first.

entries.title: tar -xzf arc.tar.gz
entries.description: Extract a .tar.gz archive (gunzip + untar in one step) into the current folder.

entries.title: tar -czf arc.tar.gz -C /path dir
entries.description: Compress with a specific base path

entries.title: tar -xf arc.tar
entries.description: Extract a plain .tar archive into the current folder.

entries.title: gzip -d <file>.gz
entries.description: Decompress a .gz file back to its original file (the same as gunzip).

entries.title: unzip arc.zip
entries.description: Extract a .zip archive into the current folder.

entries.title: 7z x arc.7z
entries.description: Extract a .7z archive (7-Zip format) into the current folder.

entries.title: xz -d <file>.xz
entries.description: Decompress a .xz file back to its original file.

entries.title: zcat file.gz
entries.description: Show a .gz file's content without extracting

entries.title: tar -czf /backup/site-$(date +%F).tar.gz /var/www/html
entries.description: Back up the website folder into a dated archive (the filename gets today's date, like site-2026-11-18.tar.gz), so each day's backup has its own name.

entries.title: crontab -r
entries.description: Delete the whole schedule (use with care)

entries.title: at 14:30
entries.description: Run once at a set time (then type the command, Ctrl+D)

entries.title: atq
entries.description: List the jobs scheduled with 'at' (one-time jobs to run later).

entries.title: sleep 1h 30m
entries.description: Pause one and a half hours

entries.title: alias
entries.description: List all the command shortcuts (aliases) defined in your current shell.

entries.title: . ~/.bashrc
entries.description: Reload your .bashrc in the current shell, so changes to it (new aliases, variables) take effect without opening a new terminal.

entries.title: cmd1 | cmd2
entries.description: Output of the first becomes input of the second

entries.title: cmd1 && cmd2
entries.description: Run the second only if the first succeeds

entries.title: cmd1 || cmd2
entries.description: Run the second only if the first fails

entries.title: cmd &> all.txt
entries.description: Output and errors together in one file

entries.title: cmd 2>&1 | less
entries.description: Send errors into the pipe too

entries.title: cmd1 | tee out.txt
entries.description: Show output + save it to a file
A shell wildcard that matches exactly one character in a filename (for example, file?.txt matches file1.txt but not file12.txt).

Exit code of the last command (0 = success)
PID of the last background process

entries.title: Ctrl+U / Ctrl+K
entries.description: Delete to start / end of line

entries.title: Tab
entries.description: The Tab key completes what you are typing — a command, a filename, or a path. Press it twice to see all matches.

entries.title: sudo !!
entries.description: Repeat the last command with sudo

entries.title: ./deploy.sh 2>&1 | tee deploy.log
entries.description: Run deploy.sh and show its output on screen while also saving it to deploy.log (2>&1 sends errors to the same stream, tee copies it to the file).

entries.title: nano <file>
entries.description: Open a file in the Nano editor — the simplest terminal editor, with its shortcuts shown at the bottom of the screen.

entries.title: Ctrl+O
entries.description: In Nano: save (write out) the file you are editing.

entries.title: Ctrl+X
entries.description: In Nano: exit the editor (it asks whether to save if you changed anything).

entries.title: Ctrl+K
entries.description: In Nano: cut (delete) the current line into the cut buffer.

entries.title: Ctrl+U
entries.description: In Nano: paste the last cut text back at the cursor.

entries.title: Ctrl+\
entries.description: In Nano: search and replace text in the file.

entries.title: Ctrl+G
entries.description: In Nano: open the help screen with all the shortcuts.

entries.title: Alt+U
entries.description: In Nano: undo the last change.

entries.title: vim <file>
entries.description: Open a file in Vim. Vim starts in normal mode — press i to type, Esc to stop typing, and :wq to save and quit.

entries.title: :q
entries.description: In Vim: quit the editor (it refuses if you have unsaved changes — use :q! to quit without saving).

entries.title: :wq
entries.description: In Vim: save the file and quit, in one step.

entries.title: dd
entries.description: In Vim (normal mode): delete the current line.

entries.title: yy
entries.description: In Vim (normal mode): copy (yank) the current line.

entries.title: p
entries.description: In Vim (normal mode): paste the copied or cut text after the cursor.

entries.title: u
entries.description: In Vim (normal mode): undo the last change.

entries.title: gg
entries.description: Go to the start of the file

entries.title: G
entries.description: Go to the end of the file

entries.title: vmstat 1
entries.description: Virtual memory and CPU stats every second

entries.title: cat /proc/cpuinfo | grep "model name"
entries.description: Show the CPU model name from the kernel's cpuinfo file.

entries.title: cat /proc/meminfo
entries.description: Show detailed memory information from the kernel: total, free, available, buffers and more.

entries.title: cat /proc/loadavg
entries.description: Show the system's load averages (1, 5 and 15 minutes) — roughly, how busy the CPU has been.

entries.title: ps aux --sort=-%mem | head -n 11
entries.description: Show the 10 processes using the most memory, sorted biggest first (the 11th line is the header).

entries.title: ssh-copy-id user@host
entries.description: Copy the public key to a server

entries.title: ssh-keygen -y -f key.pem
entries.description: Get the public key from a private key

entries.title: sudo ufw allow 80,443/tcp
entries.description: Open the web ports (80 for HTTP, 443 for HTTPS) in the UFW firewall, so the web server is reachable.

entries.title: sudo ufw deny 23/tcp
entries.description: Block port 23 (Telnet) in the UFW firewall, so nobody can connect to it.

entries.title: sudo ufw enable
entries.description: Turn the UFW firewall on (it starts blocking by your rules). Be careful over SSH: allow your SSH port first, or you can lock yourself out.

entries.title: sudo ufw delete allow 80/tcp
entries.description: Remove the firewall rule that allowed port 80, closing that port again.

entries.title: sudo iptables -L -n
entries.description: List the iptables firewall rules (numbers instead of hostnames, so it is fast and unambiguous).

entries.title: sudo chage -d 0 <user>
entries.description: Force password change on next login

entries.command: sudo ufw allow OpenSSH && sudo ufw allow 'Nginx Full' && sudo ufw --force enable
entries.title: sudo ufw allow OpenSSH && sudo ufw allow 'Nginx Full' && sudo ufw --force enable
entries.description: The safe order for turning on UFW on a web server: allow SSH first (so you don't lock yourself out), then allow the full Nginx profile (HTTP + HTTPS), then enable the firewall without asking.
entries.example: sudo ufw allow OpenSSH && sudo ufw allow 'Nginx Full' && sudo ufw --force enable

entries.title: tmux ls
entries.description: List your tmux sessions (persistent terminal sessions that keep running after you disconnect).

entries.title: Ctrl+B then C
entries.description: In tmux: create a new window inside the current session (press Ctrl+B, release, then C).

entries.title: Ctrl+B then X
entries.description: In tmux: close the current pane (press Ctrl+B, release, then X — it asks for confirmation).

entries.title: screen -ls
entries.description: List your screen sessions (persistent terminal sessions that keep running after you disconnect).

entries.title: Ctrl+A then D
entries.description: In screen: detach from the session, leaving it running in the background (press Ctrl+A, release, then D).

entries.title: Ctrl+A then C
entries.description: In screen: create a new window inside the current session (press Ctrl+A, release, then C).

entries.title: System is slow
entries.description: top, htop, free -h, uptime, ps aux --sort=-%cpu | head

entries.title: Disk is full
entries.description: df -h, du -sh /* 2>/dev/null | sort -rh | head, sudo journalctl --disk-usage

entries.title: Port unreachable
entries.description: ss -tlnp | grep <port>, sudo ufw status, curl -v localhost:<port>

entries.title: No internet
entries.description: ping 8.8.8.8, ip route, nmcli device status

entries.title: Deleted file
entries.description: lsof | grep deleted (if a process still has it open)

entries.command: uptime && free -h && df -h && systemctl --failed && ss -tlnp | head
entries.title: uptime && free -h && df -h && systemctl --failed && ss -tlnp | head

entries.example: uptime && free -h && df -h && systemctl --failed && ss -tlnp | head

entries.title: <cmd> -?
entries.description: Show the short help for any command (its syntax and parameters) by adding -? after it.

entries.title: Get-Command *process*
entries.description: Cmdlets with process in the name

entries.title: Get-Command -Verb Get
entries.description: All cmdlets with the verb Get

entries.title: Get-Module
entries.description: List the modules currently loaded in this session.

entries.title: Get-Alias
entries.description: List all command aliases (short names) available in this session.

entries.title: Get-Alias ls
entries.description: Show what the 'ls' alias points to (Get-ChildItem).

entries.title: Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser RemoteSigned
entries.description: Policy for the current user only

entries.title: $LASTEXITCODE
entries.description: Exit code of the last external program

entries.title: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\script.ps1
entries.description: Run a PowerShell script file, bypassing the execution policy for this one run (the policy itself is not changed).

entries.title: Get-ChildItem / ls / dir
entries.description: List the files and folders in the current directory (ls and dir are aliases for the same command).

entries.title: Get-ChildItem -Recurse
entries.description: List files in the current folder and all subfolders.

entries.title: Copy-Item src.txt dst.txt / cp
entries.description: Copy a file to a new location or name (cp is the short alias).

entries.title: Move-Item old.txt new.txt / mv
entries.description: Move a file to another folder, or rename it (mv is the short alias).

entries.title: Remove-Item file.txt / rm
entries.description: Delete a file permanently (rm is the short alias). No trash, no undo.

entries.title: Remove-Item -Recurse -Force dir
entries.description: Delete a directory and its contents

entries.title: Get-ChildItem -Directory | ForEach-Object {
entries.description: The start of a loop over the subfolders, to do something inside each one (the snippet continues on the next lines).

entries.title: Measure-Object Length -Sum).Sum
entries.description: Part of a snippet that totals file sizes: Measure-Object adds up the Length of each file, and .Sum gives the total.

entries.title: Get-Content file.txt -TotalCount 10
entries.description: Show only the first 10 lines of a file.

entries.title: Get-Content file.txt -Tail 10
entries.description: Show only the last 10 lines of a file — the usual way to check the end of a log.

entries.title: Out-File out.txt
entries.description: Save command output to a file

entries.title: Set-Content file.txt -Encoding utf8
entries.description: Write with UTF-8 (no BOM in PS 7)

entries.title: ConvertFrom-Json (Get-Content j.json -Raw)
entries.description: Read a JSON file as one string and convert it into a PowerShell object you can work with ($data.Name and so on).

entries.title: Select-String "error" file.log
entries.description: Search text in a file (like grep)

entries.title: Select-String -NotMatch "ok" file.log
entries.description: Lines that do NOT contain the text

entries.title: $var

entries.title: ${var name}
entries.description: Variable with a space in the name

entries.title: $env:COMPUTERNAME
entries.description: An environment variable holding this computer's name.

entries.title: $HOME
entries.description: An automatic variable holding the path to your home folder.

entries.title: $var -is [string]
entries.description: Test whether $var holds a string (true or false).

entries.title: (Get-Date).ToString("yyyy-MM-dd")
entries.description: Format the current date as year-month-day (like 2026-11-18).

entries.title: New-TimeSpan -Days 2
entries.description: Create a time span of 2 days, for date math (for example, (Get-Date) - (New-TimeSpan -Days 2)).

entries.description: Generate a random whole number from 1 to 99 (the maximum is exclusive).

entries.description: Save a user-level environment variable named MY_APP (here, pointing at C:\Tools), so it survives after the session ends.

entries.description: Array does not contain a value?

entries.title: -notin
entries.description: Value is not in an array?

entries.title: -and / -or / -not / !
entries.description: Logical operators in PowerShell: -and (both true), -or (either true), -not / ! (negation).

entries.description: A second condition in an if/elseif chain: if the age is 13 or older, the result is 'teen'.

entries.title: return <value>
entries.description: Exit a function/script with a value

entries.title: switch -Regex

entries.title: Permission error on a volume
entries.description: docker exec -u root <name> chown -R 1000:1000 /data, or check the USER in the Dockerfile

docker logs --tail 50 <name>
entries.description: Show only the last 50 lines of a container's logs. Same idea as --tail 100, but shorter — a quick glance at the most recent output.

entries.title: docker inspect <name> | grep -E "Status|Error|ExitCode"
entries.description: Show a container's low-level details (from docker inspect) and keep only the lines about its status, error or exit code — a fast health check for a crashed container.

entries.title: docker exec -it <name> sh
entries.description: Open an interactive shell inside a running container (sh is available even in minimal images that have no bash). Use it to look around or debug from the inside.

entries.title: USER node in the Dockerfile
entries.description: Run the container as a non-root user

entries.title: docker scan myapp:1.0
entries.description: Scan the image for vulnerabilities (Docker Scout)

entries.title: COPY --chown=node:node
entries.description: Correct file ownership in the image

entries.title: Secrets in Compose
entries.description: Put passwords in .env, not in the Dockerfile; in Swarm use docker secret

entries.title: --secret in build
entries.description: docker build --secret id=token,src=token.txt for build-time tokens

entries.title: Keep base images updated
entries.description: Old images have vulnerabilities; rebuild regularly

entries.command: sudo usermod -aG docker only for trusted users
entries.title: sudo usermod -aG docker only for trusted users
entries.description: Membership in the docker group equals root access

entries.title: Multi-stage build
entries.description: Build stage separate from the final stage; the final image only has the output

entries.title: Combine RUN with &&

entries.command: Clean the cache in the same layer
entries.title: Clean the cache in the same layer
entries.description: apt-get clean && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* in the same RUN

entries.title: Layer order
entries.description: Copy rarely-changing files (like package.json) first so the cache is preserved

entries.title: COPY instead of ADD
entries.description: Use ADD only when an archive must be extracted or a URL downloaded

entries.title: Specific tags
entries.description: Exact base image version: postgres:16-alpine, not postgres

entries.title: docker run -d --name web -p 8080:80 \
entries.description: Start a detached container named web publishing port 80 inside the container on port 8080 of the host (the command continues on the next line with the image).

entries.title: docker run -d --name db -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=secret \
entries.description: Start a detached Postgres container named db with its password set through an environment variable (the command continues on the next line with the image).

entries.title: docker run -d --name cache -p 6379:6379 redis:7-alpine
entries.description: Start a Redis 7 cache container named cache, publishing its default port 6379 on the host so your app can connect to localhost:6379.

entries.title: docker run --rm -v pgdata:/data -v $(pwd):/backup \
entries.description: Run a throwaway container (removed when it exits) with the pgdata volume mounted at /data and the current folder mounted at /backup — the setup for a one-off backup (the command continues on the next line).
entries.example: docker run --rm -v pgdata:/data -v $(pwd):/backup ubuntu tar czf /backup/pgdata.tar.gz /data

entries.title: ubuntu tar czf /backup/pgdata.tar.gz /data
entries.description: The second line of the one-off backup run: inside an ubuntu container, compress the contents of /data into pgdata.tar.gz in /backup (which is your current folder on the host).

entries.title: docker stop $(docker ps -aq)
entries.description: Stop every container on this host at once — docker ps -aq lists all container IDs (running and stopped) and stop acts on each. Use with care: it stops everything.

entries.title: docker volume prune -f
entries.description: Delete all unused volumes (those not attached to any container) without asking. Frees disk space, but any data in those volumes is gone.

entries.title: docker system prune -a -f --volumes
entries.description: The big cleanup: remove all stopped containers, unused networks, unused images and unused volumes without asking. Frees the most space — and deletes anything not currently in use.

entries.title: docker exec -it web sh
entries.description: Open an interactive shell inside the running 'web' container. Same as exec -it <name> sh, with the container name already filled in.

entries.title: docker cp web:/var/log/nginx/access.log ./access.log
entries.description: Copy a file out of a container to your host — here, the nginx access log from the web container into the current folder.

entries.title: docker run --rm -v $(pwd):/app -w /app node:20-alpine npm test
entries.description: Run your project's tests inside a throwaway Node container: mount the current folder at /app, work from /app, and run npm test — no Node install needed on the host, and the container is removed when done.

entries.title: docker ps -q | xargs docker inspect -f '{{.Name}} {{.NetworkSettings.IPAddress}}'
entries.description: List every running container's name and IP address: ps -q gives the IDs, and inspect prints each one's name and internal IP.

entries.title: git config --global user.name "Your Name"
entries.description: Set the name Git stamps on every commit you make on this machine. Do this once after installing Git — every commit records this name as its author.

entries.title: git config --global user.email "your.email@example.com"
entries.description: Set the email Git stamps on every commit you make on this machine. Use the email tied to your GitHub account so your commits link to your profile.

entries.title: git config --global core.editor "code --wait"
entries.description: Make VS Code Git's default editor for commit messages and rebases (the --wait flag makes Git wait until you close the tab).

entries.title: git config --global core.editor "vim"
entries.description: Make Vim Git's default editor for commit messages and rebases.

entries.title: git config --global core.editor "nano"
entries.description: Make Nano Git's default editor for commit messages and rebases — the simplest choice if you don't want to learn Vim.

entries.title: git config --list
entries.description: Show all Git settings currently in effect (user, email, editor, aliases) and where each one comes from.

entries.title: git config --global init.defaultBranch main
entries.description: Make new repositories start on a branch named 'main' instead of Git's old default 'master'.

entries.title: git config --global color.ui auto
entries.description: Turn on colors in Git's terminal output (branches, diffs, status) when the output is a terminal.

entries.title: git config --global alias.co checkout
entries.description: Create a 'co' shortcut for checkout, so you can type git co instead of git checkout.

entries.title: git config --global alias.st status
entries.description: Create a 'st' shortcut for status — the command you run most often, now two letters.

entries.title: git config --global alias.lg "log --oneline --graph --all --decorate"
entries.description: Create an 'lg' shortcut: a compact graph of your whole history, one line per commit, with branch and tag names shown.

entries.title: git init
entries.description: Turn the current folder into a Git repository, so Git starts tracking its files. Run it once, in the project's root folder.

entries.title: git init -b main
entries.description: Create a new repository whose first branch is named 'main' right away, instead of the default name.

entries.title: git clone <repository-url>
entries.description: Download a full copy of a remote repository (all files and all history) into a new folder. Use it to start working on an existing project.

entries.title: git clone -b <branch-name> <repository-url>
entries.description: Clone a repository and check out one specific branch instead of the default branch. Useful when you only need a feature branch.

entries.title: git clone --depth 1 <repository-url>
entries.description: Clone only the latest commit, skipping the rest of the history. Much faster to download, but you cannot see older commits.

entries.title: git clone git@github.com:username/repository.git
entries.description: Clone a GitHub repository over SSH (key-based login, no password prompt each time). Works once you have added your SSH key to GitHub.

entries.title: git clone https://github.com/username/repository.git
entries.description: Clone a GitHub repository over HTTPS (you sign in with a token or your credentials when asked).

entries.title: git status
entries.description: Show the state of your working files: which changed, which are staged for commit, and which are untracked. Run it constantly — it tells you what Git sees.

entries.title: git status -s
entries.description: The same status, in a short two-column form (one line per file). Faster to scan when many files changed.

entries.title: git add <filename>
entries.description: Stage one file, marking its current changes to be included in the next commit. Staging is Git's 'ready to commit' step.

entries.title: git add .
entries.description: Stage all changed and new files in the current folder and below. Quick, but check git status first so you don't stage something by accident.

entries.title: git add -A
entries.description: Stage everything in the whole repository: new, modified and deleted files. The most complete way to stage.

entries.title: git add -u
entries.description: Stage changes to files Git already tracks (modified and deleted), but ignore brand-new untracked files.

entries.title: git add -p
entries.description: Stage your changes piece by piece: Git shows each hunk and asks whether to stage it. Use it to split one file's changes across two commits.

entries.title: git commit -m "Your commit message"
entries.description: Save the staged changes as a new commit with a short message describing them. The message is how future-you understands what changed.

entries.title: git commit -am "Your commit message"
entries.description: Stage all tracked-file changes and commit them in one step (new untracked files are still left out). A shortcut for add -u plus commit.

entries.title: git commit
entries.description: Commit the staged changes and open your editor to write the message. Use it for longer messages that don't fit on one line.

entries.title: git commit --amend -m "New message"
entries.description: Replace the last commit's message (and optionally its contents) with a corrected one. Only safe before you push.

entries.title: git add <forgotten-file>
entries.description: Stage a file you forgot to include in the last commit, so you can fold it in with --amend instead of making a new commit.

entries.title: git commit --amend --no-edit
entries.description: Fold the newly staged changes into the last commit without changing its message. Use it right after adding a forgotten file.

entries.title: git commit -m "message" --author="Name <email>"
entries.description: Create a commit recorded under a different author name and email. The commit itself is the same; only the authorship shown in the log changes.

entries.title: git commit -m "message" --date="2024-01-01 12:00:00"
entries.description: Create a commit stamped with a custom date instead of now. Useful when importing old work; the commit content is unchanged, only its recorded date.

entries.title: git log
entries.description: Show the commit history of the current branch, newest first, with hash, author, date and message for each commit.

entries.title: git log --oneline
entries.description: The same history, one short line per commit (short hash + message). The quickest way to scan what happened.

entries.title: git log --graph --oneline --all
entries.description: Draw your history as a branching graph across all branches, one line per commit. The best way to see how branches split and merged.

entries.title: git log -p
entries.description: Show the history with the actual changes (patch) of each commit, so you can see what each commit did, not just its message.

entries.title: git log -n 5
entries.description: Show only the last 5 commits. Use it when you just need a quick look at recent history.

entries.title: git log --author="Name"
entries.description: Show only the commits made by one author. Useful to review what a teammate (or you) did.

entries.title: git log --since="2024-01-01" --until="2024-12-31"
entries.description: Show only the commits made between two dates — here, all of 2024. Use it to review a time period.

entries.title: git log --stat
entries.description: Show the history with a summary of which files each commit changed and how many lines were added or removed.

entries.title: git log --name-only
entries.description: Show the history listing only the file names each commit touched, without the line counts.

entries.title: git log -p <filename>
entries.description: Show the full change history of one file, with the actual diffs, so you can trace how that file evolved.

entries.title: git blame <filename>
entries.description: Show a file with every line annotated by the commit and author that last changed it. The fastest way to ask 'who wrote this line, and why'.

entries.title: git blame -L 10,20 <filename>
entries.description: Blame only lines 10 to 20 of a file, instead of the whole file. Use it when you care about one small section.

entries.title: git show <commit-hash>
entries.description: Show everything about one commit: its message, author, date, and the full diff of what it changed.

entries.title: git show <commit-hash> --stat
entries.description: Show one commit's summary only (which files changed and by how much), without the full diff.

entries.title: git branch
entries.description: List the local branches in this repository. The current branch is marked with a star.

entries.title: git branch -a
entries.description: List all branches, local and remote-tracking. Shows you what exists on the remote too.

entries.title: git branch -v
entries.description: List local branches with the last commit on each, so you can see at a glance where every branch points.

entries.title: git branch --merged
entries.description: List the branches already merged into the current branch — the safe candidates for deleting.

entries.title: git branch --no-merged
entries.description: List the branches NOT yet merged into the current branch — work that would be lost if you deleted them.

entries.title: git branch <branch-name>
entries.description: Create a new branch pointing at your current commit, without switching to it.

entries.title: git branch <branch-name> <commit-hash>
entries.description: Create a new branch pointing at a specific older commit, instead of the current one.

entries.title: git switch <branch-name>
entries.description: Switch to another branch. Your working files change to match that branch.

entries.title: git checkout <branch-name>
entries.description: Switch to another branch (the older command — git switch is the modern replacement; checkout still works the same way).

entries.title: git switch -c <branch-name>
entries.description: Create a new branch and switch to it in one step. The usual way to start new work.

entries.title: git checkout -b <branch-name>
entries.description: Create a new branch and switch to it (the older command — git switch -c is the modern replacement).

entries.title: git switch -c <branch-name> origin/<remote-branch>
entries.description: Create a local branch tracking a branch that exists on the remote, and switch to it. Use it to start working on someone else's branch.

entries.title: git branch -m <new-name>
entries.description: Rename the current branch to a new name.

entries.title: git branch -m <old-name> <new-name>
entries.description: Rename a branch (not necessarily the current one) from its old name to a new name.

entries.title: git branch -d <branch-name>
entries.description: Delete a branch that has already been merged. Git refuses if the branch still has unmerged work.

entries.title: git branch -D <branch-name>
entries.description: Force-delete a branch even if it has unmerged work. Only use it when you are sure the work is not needed.

entries.title: git push origin --delete <branch-name>
entries.description: Delete a branch on the remote (origin). The local branch stays until you delete it separately.

entries.title: git branch --set-upstream-to=origin/<branch>
entries.description: Link the current branch to a remote branch, so plain git pull and git push know where to fetch from and push to.

entries.title: git branch --show-current
entries.description: Print just the name of the current branch. Useful in scripts.

entries.title: git merge <branch-name>
entries.description: Merge another branch into the current one, combining both histories. If both sides changed the same lines, Git asks you to resolve the conflict.

entries.title: git merge <branch-name> -m "Merge message"
entries.description: Merge a branch with a custom merge-commit message, instead of Git's default one.

entries.title: git merge --no-ff <branch-name>
entries.description: Merge with an explicit merge commit, even when a fast-forward would be possible. Keeps the branch visible in history.

entries.title: git merge --ff-only <branch-name>
entries.description: Merge only if it can be a fast-forward (no new commit). Refuses instead of creating a merge commit.

entries.title: git merge --abort
entries.description: Give up on a merge in progress (usually because of conflicts) and return the files to how they were before the merge started.

entries.title: git diff
entries.description: Show the unstaged changes in your working files — what you changed since the last commit, line by line.

entries.title: git merge --continue
entries.description: Continue a merge after you resolved its conflicts (stage the resolved files first, then run this).

entries.title: git merge-base <branch1> <branch2>
entries.description: Print the hash of the commit where two branches last shared history (their common ancestor). Useful to understand what a merge will combine.

entries.title: git merge --squash <branch-name>
entries.description: Fold a whole branch's changes into your working files as one uncommitted change, without recording the branch's individual commits. Commit once to keep a single clean commit.

entries.title: git rebase <base-branch>
entries.description: Replay your current branch's commits on top of another branch, so your work sits on the latest base. It rewrites your commits' hashes — only do this on unpushed work.

entries.title: git rebase -i HEAD~<number-of-commits>
entries.description: Open an interactive rebase for your last few commits, to reorder, squash, or rewrite their messages. The main tool for cleaning up history before pushing.

entries.title: git rebase -i <commit-hash>^
entries.description: Open an interactive rebase starting at the parent of one commit, so that commit itself is included in the list you can edit.

entries.title: git rebase --onto <new-base> <old-base> <branch>
entries.description: Move a branch (or part of it) onto a different base commit. The advanced way to transplant commits from one base to another.

entries.title: git rebase --continue
entries.description: Continue a rebase after you resolved a conflict (stage the resolved files first).

entries.title: git rebase --skip
entries.description: Skip the current commit during a rebase (for example, if its changes are already in the base) and move on to the next one.

entries.title: git rebase --abort
entries.description: Give up on a rebase in progress and return everything to how it was before the rebase started.

entries.title: git rebase --autostash
entries.description: Rebase while automatically stashing your uncommitted changes first and restoring them after. Use it when you have dirty files but want to rebase anyway.

entries.title: git pull --rebase
entries.description: Fetch the latest changes and replay your local commits on top of them (instead of a merge commit). Keeps history linear.

entries.title: git pull --rebase=interactive
entries.description: Pull with a rebase, and open the interactive editor so you can reorder or squash your commits while pulling.

entries.title: git config --global pull.rebase true
entries.description: Make every git pull use rebase by default, so you never get surprise merge commits from pulling.

entries.title: git remote -v
entries.description: List the remotes of this repository with their URLs (fetch and push). Shows you where origin actually points.

entries.title: git remote add <name> <url>
entries.description: Add a new remote under a short name, so you can fetch from and push to another repository.

entries.title: git remote add origin https://github.com/user/repo.git
entries.description: Add a remote named 'origin' pointing at your GitHub repository — the standard first remote for a project.

entries.title: git remote remove <name>
entries.description: Remove a remote and all of its remote-tracking branches from this repository.

entries.title: git remote rename <old-name> <new-name>
entries.description: Rename a remote and update all of its remote-tracking branches to match.

entries.title: git remote show <name>
entries.description: Show details about a remote: its URL, which branches it tracks, and whether your local branches are ahead or behind.

entries.title: git fetch <remote>
entries.description: Download the latest commits and branches from a remote without changing your working files. Safe to run any time — it never touches your work.

entries.title: git fetch origin
entries.description: Download the latest commits and branches from origin without changing your working files.

entries.title: git fetch --all
entries.description: Fetch from every remote this repository has, not just origin.

entries.title: git fetch origin <branch>
entries.description: Fetch only one branch from origin, instead of everything.

entries.title: git pull origin <branch>
entries.description: Fetch a branch from origin and merge it into your current branch in one step.

entries.title: git pull --rebase origin <branch>
entries.description: Fetch a branch from origin and replay your local commits on top of it, instead of merging. Keeps history linear.

entries.title: git push origin <branch>
entries.description: Upload your branch's commits to origin, so others can see them (or so your work is backed up).

entries.title: git push -u origin <branch>
entries.description: Push a branch and link it to the same-named branch on origin, so future plain git push and git pull just work.

entries.title: git push --all origin
entries.description: Push all of your local branches to origin at once.

entries.title: git push --tags origin
entries.description: Push your local tags to origin (tags are not pushed by a normal push).

entries.title: git push --force origin <branch>
entries.description: Overwrite the remote branch with your local history, discarding any commits on the remote that you don't have. Dangerous on shared branches — prefer --force-with-lease.

entries.title: git push --force-with-lease origin <branch>
entries.description: Like --force, but refuses if someone else pushed to the remote branch since you last fetched. The safer way to rewrite a branch you already pushed.

entries.title: git push origin --delete <branch>
entries.description: Delete a branch on the remote (origin). The local branch stays until you delete it separately.

entries.title: git push origin <local-branch>:<remote-branch>
entries.description: Push your local branch to a differently-named branch on the remote.

entries.title: git restore --staged <filename>
entries.description: Unstage a file, keeping its changes in your working files. The changes stay — they just won't be in the next commit.

entries.title: git reset HEAD <filename>
entries.description: Unstage a file (the older command — git restore --staged is the modern replacement). The file's changes stay in your working files.

entries.title: git restore <filename>
entries.description: Throw away the uncommitted changes in one file, restoring it to the last commit. The changes are gone for good.

entries.title: git checkout -- <filename>
entries.description: Throw away the uncommitted changes in one file (the older command — git restore is the modern replacement). The changes are gone for good.

entries.title: git restore .
entries.description: Throw away all uncommitted changes in the current folder and below. Use with care — everything uncommitted is lost.

entries.title: git reset --soft HEAD~1
entries.description: Undo the last commit but keep all its changes staged, so you can commit them again differently (for example, split into two commits).

entries.title: git reset --hard HEAD~1
entries.description: Undo the last commit and throw away its changes completely. The commit and its work are gone — only use it on unpushed commits.

entries.title: git reset --hard <commit-hash>
entries.description: Move the branch back to one specific commit and discard everything after it. The later commits and their changes are gone.

entries.title: git revert <commit-hash>
entries.description: Undo one commit by creating a NEW commit that reverses its changes. The safe way to undo work that is already pushed — history stays intact.

entries.title: git revert <commit-hash1>..<commit-hash2>
entries.description: Revert a whole range of commits at once, creating new commits that undo them. Use it to back out a series of changes safely.

entries.title: git revert -n <commit-hash>
entries.description: Revert a commit but leave the reversed changes staged instead of committing them, so you can adjust them before committing.

entries.title: git clean -n
entries.description: Dry run (show what would be deleted)

entries.title: git stash
entries.description: Shelve your uncommitted changes and return to a clean working folder, so you can switch branches or pull without committing half-done work.

entries.title: git stash push -m "Stash message"
entries.description: Stash your changes with a label describing them, so you can tell your stashes apart later in the list.

entries.title: git stash -u
entries.description: Stash your changes including untracked files (new files Git doesn't know yet). A plain stash leaves untracked files behind.

entries.title: git stash --include-untracked
entries.description: Stash your changes including untracked files — the long form of git stash -u.

entries.title: git stash list
entries.description: List all your stashes, newest first, with their messages.

entries.title: git stash apply
entries.description: Bring back the most recent stash's changes into your working files, but keep the stash saved in the list too.

entries.title: git stash apply stash@{2}
entries.description: Bring back one specific stash (here, the third one in the list) without removing it from the list.

entries.title: git stash pop
entries.description: Bring back the most recent stash's changes and remove it from the list. The usual way to resume stashed work.

entries.title: git stash pop stash@{1}
entries.description: Bring back one specific stash (here, the second one) and remove it from the list.

entries.title: git stash drop stash@{0}
entries.description: Delete one stash from the list without applying it. Its changes are gone.

entries.title: git stash clear
entries.description: Delete all stashes at once. Everything stashed is gone — only do this when you are sure.

entries.title: git stash show stash@{0}
entries.description: Show a summary of what one stash changed (which files, how many lines) without applying it.

entries.title: git stash show -p stash@{0}
entries.description: Show the full diff of what one stash changed, so you can decide whether to apply it.

entries.title: git stash branch <branch-name> stash@{0}
entries.description: Create a new branch from one stash and apply the stash there. Use it when a stash belongs on its own branch.

entries.title: git tag
entries.description: List all tags in this repository (usually version numbers like v1.0.0).

entries.title: git tag -l "v1.*"
entries.description: List only the tags matching a pattern — here, all v1.x versions.

entries.title: git tag <tag-name>
entries.description: Create a lightweight tag (just a name) on the current commit, marking it as a version or milestone.

entries.title: git tag -a <tag-name> -m "Tag message"
entries.description: Create an annotated tag: a full object with a message, tagger and date. The proper way to mark a release version.

entries.title: git tag <tag-name> <commit-hash>
entries.description: Create a tag on one specific older commit, instead of the current one.

entries.title: git push origin <tag-name>
entries.description: Push one tag to origin (tags are not pushed by a normal push).

entries.title: git push origin --tags
entries.description: Push all of your local tags to origin at once.

entries.title: git tag -d <tag-name>
entries.description: Delete a tag locally. The remote copy stays until you delete it there too.

entries.title: git push origin --delete <tag-name>
entries.description: Delete a tag on the remote.

entries.title: git push origin :refs/tags/<tag-name>
entries.description: Delete a tag on the remote using the older refspec form (the --delete form above is the modern way).

entries.title: git show <tag-name>
entries.description: Show the commit a tag points to, with its message and changes.

entries.title: git checkout <tag-name>
entries.description: Check out the commit a tag points to. You land in a detached HEAD state — look, don't commit here.

entries.title: git checkout -b <branch-name> <tag-name>
entries.description: Create a branch starting from a tag, so you can work from that version (for example, a hotfix on an old release).

entries.title: git diff --staged
entries.description: Show the changes you have staged (what the next commit will contain), line by line.

entries.title: git diff --cached
entries.description: Show the staged changes — the same as git diff --staged (an older name for the same thing).

entries.title: git diff <branch1>..<branch2>
entries.description: Show the difference between the tips of two branches — what changed from one to the other.

entries.title: git diff <commit1> <commit2>
entries.description: Show the difference between two specific commits.

entries.title: git diff <filename>
entries.description: Show the unstaged changes in one file only.

entries.title: git diff --word-diff
entries.description: Show differences word by word instead of line by line — easier to spot small edits inside long lines.

entries.title: git diff --color
entries.description: Show the diff with colors (added lines green, removed lines red), even when piping the output.

entries.title: git diff --stat
entries.description: Show a diff as a summary only: which files changed and how many lines were added or removed.

entries.title: git diff --name-only
entries.description: Show a diff as just the list of changed file names, nothing else. Useful in scripts.

entries.title: git diff <branch>
entries.description: Show the difference between your current branch and another branch.

entries.title: git diff origin/main
entries.description: Show how your work differs from the latest main on the remote — what you would get (or send) on a pull or push.

entries.title: git cherry-pick <commit-hash>
entries.description: Copy one commit from another branch onto your current branch, as a new commit with the same changes.

entries.title: git cherry-pick -e <commit-hash>
entries.description: Cherry-pick a commit but open the editor first, so you can adjust its message before committing.

entries.title: git cherry-pick -n <commit-hash>
entries.description: Cherry-pick a commit's changes into your working files without committing them, so you can adjust before committing.

entries.title: git cherry-pick <start-commit>..<end-commit>
entries.description: Cherry-pick a whole range of commits onto your current branch, oldest first.

entries.title: git cherry-pick --continue
entries.description: Continue a cherry-pick after you resolved a conflict (stage the resolved files first).

entries.title: git cherry-pick --abort
entries.description: Give up on a cherry-pick in progress and return the files to how they were before it started.

entries.title: git cherry-pick --skip
entries.description: Skip the current commit during a cherry-pick (for example, if its changes are already here) and move on.

entries.title: git bisect start
entries.description: Start a bisect session: Git will binary-search your history to find the exact commit that introduced a bug.

entries.title: git bisect bad
entries.description: During a bisect, mark the current commit as broken. Git then checks out a commit halfway back to narrow the search.

entries.title: git bisect good <commit-hash>
entries.description: During a bisect, mark one specific commit as working, so Git only searches the commits after it.

entries.title: git bisect good
entries.description: During a bisect, mark the current commit as working. Git narrows the search toward the broken side.

entries.title: git bisect reset
entries.description: End a bisect session and return to the branch you were on before it started.

entries.title: git bisect visualize
entries.description: During a bisect, open a graphical view of the commits still under suspicion.

entries.title: git submodule add <repository-url> <path>
entries.description: Add another repository as a sub-folder of this one (a submodule), so you can include a library while keeping its history separate.

entries.title: git submodule add https://github.com/user/repo.git libs/repo
entries.description: Add a GitHub repository as a submodule under libs/repo in this project.

entries.title: git submodule init
entries.description: Initialize the submodules recorded in this repository (register them in your local config) after a fresh clone.

entries.title: git submodule update
entries.description: Check out the recorded commit of each submodule, so their contents match what this repository expects.

entries.title: git submodule update --recursive
entries.description: Update submodules and their own submodules too, all the way down.

entries.title: git clone --recursive <repository-url>
entries.description: Clone a repository and its submodules in one go, instead of cloning and then initializing them separately.

entries.title: git submodule update --remote
entries.description: Update each submodule to the latest commit on its own remote branch, instead of the commit recorded here.

entries.title: git submodule status
entries.description: List the submodules with the commit each one is currently on, and whether it matches the recorded one.

entries.title: git submodule deinit <path>
entries.description: Remove a submodule's working files and unregister it locally (the record stays in the repository until you remove it there too).

entries.title: git rm <path>
entries.description: Remove a file or a submodule path from the repository and stage the removal, so the next commit records it as deleted.

entries.title: git worktree add <path> <branch>
entries.description: Check out a second branch into a separate folder, so you can work on two branches at once without switching or stashing.

entries.title: git worktree add ../project-branch feature-branch
entries.description: Check out the feature-branch branch into the ../project-branch folder, as a second working copy of this repository.

entries.title: git worktree add <path> <commit-hash>
entries.description: Check out one specific commit into a separate folder (detached HEAD), to inspect or test old code without disturbing your main folder.

entries.title: git worktree list
entries.description: List all worktrees of this repository, with the branch each one has checked out.

entries.title: git worktree remove <path>
entries.description: Remove a worktree folder and its checkout. Make sure its changes are committed or stashed first.

entries.title: git worktree move <old-path> <new-path>
entries.description: Move a worktree to a different folder, keeping its branch and state.

entries.title: git worktree repair
entries.description: Fix worktree records after you moved or renamed their folders by hand, so Git finds them again.

entries.title: ls .git/hooks/
entries.description: List the hook scripts in this repository — sample hooks end in .sample, active ones are the same name without it.

entries.title: mv .git/hooks/pre-commit.sample .git/hooks/pre-commit
entries.description: Activate the sample pre-commit hook by renaming it (dropping .sample). It will run before every commit from now on.

entries.title: echo '#!/bin/sh
entries.description: The first line of a hook script: write the shell shebang into the hook file (the command continues with the hook body and a redirect into .git/hooks/pre-commit).

entries.title: npm run lint
entries.description: Run the project's lint script (the command a pre-commit hook usually runs to check your code before a commit is allowed).

entries.title: chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
entries.description: Make the pre-commit hook executable, so Git can actually run it. Without this step the hook is ignored.

entries.title: git grep "search-text"
entries.description: Search the text of every tracked file for a phrase, showing the file and line of each match — like grep, but only for files Git tracks.

entries.title: git log -S "text" --oneline
entries.description: Find the commits that added or removed a specific string (the pickaxe search). Shows which commit introduced or deleted that text.

entries.title: git log -G "pattern" --oneline
entries.description: Find the commits whose diffs match a pattern (a regular expression), instead of an exact string. More flexible than -S.

entries.title: git ls-tree -r <commit-hash>
entries.description: List every file in a commit, recursively, with its mode, type and blob hash. A low-level look at what a commit contains.

entries.title: git archive --format=zip HEAD > archive.zip
entries.description: Export the current commit as a zip file of its files (no .git folder), for sharing a snapshot of the code.

entries.title: git archive --format=tar HEAD > archive.tar
entries.description: Export the current commit as a tar file of its files (no .git folder), for sharing a snapshot of the code.

entries.title: git count-objects -v
entries.description: Show statistics about the repository's object store (how many objects, how much disk they use, how packed they are).

entries.title: git gc
entries.description: Clean up the repository: compress loose objects, prune unreachable ones, and make Git faster. Safe to run occasionally.

entries.title: git fsck
entries.description: Check the repository for corruption — dangling or missing objects — and report any problems it finds.

entries.title: git reflog
entries.description: Show the history of where HEAD pointed (every checkout, commit, reset and rebase), including commits that are no longer on any branch. The safety net for recovering lost work.

entries.title: git reflog show <branch>
entries.description: Show the reflog of one specific branch, instead of HEAD's — every position that branch has pointed to.

entries.title: git blame -e -L <start>,<end> <file>
entries.description: Blame a line range of a file and show each line author's email address, instead of just the name.

entries.title: git status --ignored
entries.description: Show the status including ignored files, so you can see what .gitignore is hiding.

entries.title: git rev-list --objects --all | sort -k 2 > all-files.txt
entries.description: List every object in the repository's history with its file name, sorted, and save it to all-files.txt. Useful to find which big files are bloating the repo.

entries.title: git config --global alias.lga "log --graph --pretty=format:'%C(red)%h%C(reset) - %C(yellow)%d%C(reset) %s %C(green)(%cr) %C(blue)<%an>%C(reset)' --abbrev-commit --all"
entries.description: Create an 'lga' shortcut: a colorful, compact graph log showing short hash, decorations, message, relative date and author for all branches.

entries.title: git config --global alias.unstage "reset HEAD --"
entries.description: Create an 'unstage' shortcut: unstage files with git unstage <file>, instead of the longer reset command.

entries.title: git config --global alias.last "log -1 HEAD"
entries.description: Create a 'last' shortcut: show only the most recent commit.

entries.title: git config --global alias.visual "!gitk"
entries.description: Create a 'visual' shortcut that opens gitk, Git's graphical history viewer, from the command line.

entries.title: git config --global alias.hist "log --pretty=format:'%C(yellow)%h%C(reset) %C(green)%ad%C(reset) | %s %C(blue)[%an]%C(reset) %C(red)%d%C(reset)' --date=short"
entries.description: Create a 'hist' shortcut: a readable one-line-per-commit log with short date, message, author and decorations.

entries.title: git config --global alias.s "status -s"
entries.description: Create an 's' shortcut for the short status — the fastest way to check what changed.

entries.title: git config --global alias.dc "diff --cached"
entries.description: Create a 'dc' shortcut for the staged diff (diff --cached).

entries.title: echo "node_modules/
entries.description: Part of a command that writes ignore patterns into .gitignore (the line continues with the rest of the pattern and a redirect into .gitignore).

entries.title: .env
entries.description: A .gitignore pattern: never commit environment files — they hold secrets like API keys and passwords.

entries.title: *.log
entries.description: A .gitignore pattern: ignore all log files, in any folder.

entries.title: dist/
entries.description: A .gitignore pattern: ignore the build output folder (it is generated, not source).

entries.title: build/
entries.description: A .gitignore pattern: ignore the build output folder (it is generated, not source).

entries.title: .DS_Store
entries.description: A .gitignore pattern: ignore macOS Finder metadata files.

entries.title: *.tmp
entries.description: A .gitignore pattern: ignore all temporary files.

entries.title: .vscode/
entries.description: A .gitignore pattern: ignore personal VS Code settings (don't commit your editor setup).

entries.title: .idea/
entries.description: A .gitignore pattern: ignore JetBrains IDE settings (don't commit your editor setup).

entries.title: coverage/
entries.description: A .gitignore pattern: ignore test-coverage reports (they are generated).

entries.title: .nyc_output/
entries.description: A .gitignore pattern: ignore the raw coverage data folder (it is generated).

entries.title: " > .gitignore
entries.description: The tail of an echo command that writes a pattern into .gitignore — the closing quote and redirect of the line started above.

entries.title: git rm --cached <filename>
entries.description: Stop tracking a file without deleting it from your disk — use it after adding a file to .gitignore, so Git stops tracking it but the file stays.

entries.title: echo "<filename>" >> .gitignore
entries.description: Append a file name to .gitignore, so Git stops showing it as untracked. Use >> (append), not > (overwrite).

entries.title: git config --global core.excludesfile ~/.gitignore_global
entries.description: Set a global ignore file that applies to every repository on this machine (for files you never want to commit anywhere, like .DS_Store).

entries.title: git push --force origin main
entries.description: Force-push to main, overwriting its history on the remote. Extremely dangerous on a shared main branch — almost never what you want.

entries.title: git push origin --delete main
entries.description: Delete the main branch on the remote. Dangerous — this removes the branch everyone works from.

entries.title: git rebase -i HEAD~10
entries.description: Open an interactive rebase for the last 10 commits to rewrite, reorder or squash them. Rewrites history — only do this on commits you haven't pushed.

entries.title: git filter-repo --path large-file.zip --invert-paths
entries.description: Rewrite history to remove a file (here, large-file.zip) from every commit. Rewrites all history — everyone must re-clone afterwards.

entries.title: Initialize repo
entries.description: Create a new Git repository in the current folder — run: git init.

entries.title: Check status
entries.description: See which files changed, staged or untracked — run: git status.

entries.title: Stage file
entries.description: Add a file to the staging area before committing — run: git add <file>.

entries.title: Apply stash
entries.description: Restore the most recently stashed changes — run: git stash pop.

entries.title: Diff
entries.description: Show unstaged changes in your working files — run: git diff.
